labels.note: Heap stays ordered by expires; only tie ordering among equal expiries changes, visible in iteration order.
The `in` operator converts None to False, so only calling __contains__ directly could tell them apart.
Heap gets rebuilt on nearly every expire(): a performance regression, but results stay correct.
Public popitem returns None instead of the evicted (key, value) pair; eviction still happens.
New links get count 2, so each insert makes a separate link; count order breaks and frequently used keys get evicted.
Wrong merge condition skips counts or duplicates links, which distorts frequencies and can cause wrong evictions.
Counts jump by 2, which creates duplicate-count links, breaks list order, and can evict wrongly.
Touched key moves to a lower count on a common path, which corrupts frequency order and eviction.
